name: Desk clock with reminders
summary: A big clock window with the date and your reminders: add one for a time (once, daily, weekly or monthly), and it pops up and beeps when it's due. A first real Python app.
cheap: Any computer with Python, including a Raspberry Pi on an old screen.

guide.overview: A window with a big clock, the date, and reminders. The clock redraws itself every second with tkinter's after() (never a sleep, which would freeze the window). Reminders are kept in a file by the Reminders block, so they survive restarting the computer; every second the app asks which are due and pops them up with a beep.

files.why: The window: the clock labels, the reminder form and list, and tick(), which runs every second.

points.note: The heartbeat: update the clock, check due reminders, then ask tkinter to call tick again in (just under) a second.
Waits until the next whole second, so the clock never drifts or skips.
Reminders whose time has come; repeating ones move on to their next time automatically.

guide.starter:
"""Desk clock with reminders: you build it step by step."""
import datetime as dt
import os
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox, ttk
# archie:imports
from lib.reminders import Reminders

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

lessons.title: A ticking clock
lessons.explain: A window program spends its life in mainloop(), waiting for things to happen. To do something every second you don't loop or sleep (that freezes the window); you ask tkinter to call a function again later with after(ms, function).
lessons.task: Make a Tk window with a big Label (font size 64). Write tick() that sets the label to the time as HH:MM:SS (datetime.now().strftime) and then calls root.after(1000, tick). Call tick() once and then root.mainloop().
lessons.check: Running it opens a window whose clock ticks every second.
lessons.code:
root = tk.Tk()
clock = tk.Label(root, font=("Segoe UI", 64, "bold"))
clock.pack(padx=30, pady=20)

def tick():
    clock.config(text=dt.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S"))
    root.after(1000, tick)

tick()
root.mainloop()

lessons.title: The date
lessons.explain: strftime turns a date into text: %A is the weekday, %d the day, %B the month name, %Y the year.
lessons.task: Add a second, smaller label under the clock showing the date like Friday 02 October 2026, updated in tick().
lessons.check: The date shows under the time.
lessons.code:
date = tk.Label(root, font=("Segoe UI", 16))
date.pack()
# in tick():
date.config(text=dt.datetime.now().strftime("%A %d %B %Y"))

lessons.title: Add reminders
lessons.explain: The Reminders block stores reminders in a JSON file, so they're still there tomorrow. You add one with a time like 2026-04-01 08:00 and an optional repeat.
lessons.task: Make rem = Reminders(os.path.join(HERE, "data", "reminders.json")). Add an Entry for the time, an Entry for the text and a button that calls rem.add(time, text). Show a messagebox error if the time isn't in the right format (rem.add raises ValueError).
lessons.check: Adding a reminder works; a badly written time shows an error instead of crashing.

lessons.title: Pop up when due
lessons.explain: Every tick, ask the Reminders block which reminders are due. Show each one and beep. Repeating ones move on to their next time by themselves.
lessons.task: In tick(), loop over rem.due(): root.bell() and messagebox.showinfo("Reminder", r["text"]). Add a Listbox showing rem.upcoming() and refresh it after adding.
lessons.check: A reminder set a minute ahead pops up when its time comes.
